- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high for 2–4 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤ -0.5) within 5 days, model overcorrects downward; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to offset mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; increase forecast by 1–2% for 3–7 days.
- If recent 18-day history shows strong upward trend, model often fails to capture momentum; apply 1–2% upward adjustment to forecast for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (±0.3–0.5), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by 0.5–1.0% downward for 3–5 days.
